description: Twenty realistic director-interview utterances labeled with ideal slot extraction outputs. This dataset is scoped to extraction accuracy only: slot status, slot value correctness, and slot precision.
notes: Each task is a single-turn extraction case unless otherwise noted.
expected.slotValues are grader-friendly checks against JSON.stringify(slot_states.value).
perfectOutput.slot_updates is the human-readable reference answer for the ideal extraction.
Values use director-layer slot paths from lib/interview/director/slot-schema.ts.

tasks.description: Director names a process, cadence, systems of record, and a shadow spreadsheet.
turns: We run promotion management every Monday. Salesforce is our system of record, but pricing gets finalized in a shared Google Sheet before it goes to NetSuite.

tasks.description: Multi-turn context: second utterance uses a pronoun and must attach owner/volume/handoff to the process from turn one.
turns: Renewal review is one of our bigger workflows; it starts when Salesforce flags an account 90 days before contract end.
RevOps handles it, about 80 a week, and Finance only gets involved when discount approvals are over 20 percent.

value.trigger: Salesforce flags an account 90 days before contract end

tasks.description: Director describes a support process with pain points and handoffs.
turns: Customer escalation intake starts when a Zendesk ticket is marked urgent. Support Ops triages it, then Engineering gets pulled in through Jira if there is a product defect. The painful part is duplicate entry between Zendesk and Jira.

pain_points: duplicate entry between Zendesk and Jira

tasks.description: Hedged frequency should be partial while definite systems and controls are filled.
turns: Month-end close is run by Accounting, I think it's monthly but I'd need to confirm the exact cadence. NetSuite is definitely the system, the checklist is in Excel, and manual journal entries require controller approval.

value.uncertainty: director said exact cadence needs confirmation

controls: manual journal entries require controller approval

tasks.description: Procurement process includes boundaries, approvals, handoffs, and friction.
turns: Purchase request approval starts with a department manager submitting a request in Coupa. Procurement reviews vendor risk, Legal reviews anything over $50k, and delays usually happen waiting for budget owner approval.

value.trigger: department manager submits a request in Coupa

pain_points: delays waiting for budget owner approval

tasks.description: Planning process with inputs, systems, volume, KPIs, and variants.
turns: Demand forecasting is monthly. Planning pulls sales history from Snowflake, then category managers adjust the forecast in Excel for new launches. Forecast accuracy and stockout rate are the two KPIs we track.

variants: category managers adjust the forecast in Excel for new launches

tasks.description: HR process with owner, systems, handoffs, controls, and documentation.
turns: Employee onboarding is owned by People Ops. The workflow begins when a signed offer hits Workday, then IT provisions Okta and a laptop, and hiring managers complete a checklist in Notion. We run it for about 25 new hires a month.

tasks.description: AP exception process with systems, owner, pain point, and SPOF risk.
turns: Invoice exception handling sits with AP Operations. About 40 invoices a day get kicked out of NetSuite because the PO or receipt is missing, and Maria is the only person who knows which warehouse managers to chase.

people.name: Maria
people.relationship: single point of failure for warehouse manager chase paths

pain_points: invoices kicked out because PO or receipt is missing

spofs: Maria is the only person who knows which warehouse managers to chase

tasks.description: System context only; should not invent a process.
turns: We mostly use Salesforce as our CRM, and Slack is where people talk about account issues.

tasks.description: Director explicitly lacks process detail; should mark unknown rather than invent.
turns: I don't actually know who owns that process or how often it happens. I would need to check with the operations team.

value.unknown_reason: director does not know who owns it
director does not know how often it happens

tasks.description: Director names three processes in one utterance; all should be captured as breadth inventory.
turns: My team owns renewals, customer escalations, and demand forecasting. Renewals are weekly, escalations happen daily, and forecasting is monthly.
tasks.trackingIssue: PLAN.md gap 7.1: runDirectorTurn only handles the first recordProcess tool call

tasks.description: Common aliases should be accepted in value labels.
turns: Renewals start in SFDC, then the team updates a G Sheet that Finance uses for the weekly forecast.

dependencies: Finance uses the Google Sheet for the weekly forecast

tasks.description: Meeting cadence without a business process should not become a candidate process.
turns: We have a weekly leadership meeting where people talk through metrics, but it is not really a workflow and there is no system involved.

value.unknown_reason: director said there is no system involved

tasks.description: Single utterance contains corrected frequency; ideal output preserves correction without conflicting status.
turns: The inventory reconciliation used to run monthly, sorry, it is weekly now. Warehouse Ops owns it and they do the review in NetSuite.

tasks.description: Payroll process with compliance exposure and strict control.
turns: Payroll exception review is high-risk for us. HR Ops owns it, it runs biweekly in Workday, and any off-cycle payment over $5,000 needs CFO approval because of SOX controls.

controls: off-cycle payment over $5,000 needs CFO approval

tasks.description: Healthcare operations process with PHI/compliance risk, SLAs, and exception handling.
turns: Prior authorization for oncology meds is handled by Patient Access. It runs daily in Epic and CoverMyMeds. Missing clinical notes can delay treatment, and HIPAA requires that only authorized staff access the patient record.

pain_points: missing clinical notes can delay treatment

controls: only authorized staff access the patient record

tasks.description: Security incident process with severity, systems, handoffs, and SLA.
turns: Security incident triage starts in PagerDuty when a Sev1 alert fires. The SOC owns the first 15 minutes, then Legal and Communications join if customer data may be exposed. We track time to containment.

tasks.description: Regulatory reporting with compliance controls, deadline, systems, and SPOF.
turns: Quarterly regulatory reporting is owned by Compliance Operations. Data comes from Snowflake, gets reconciled in Excel, and must be filed by the 10th business day. Priya is the only reviewer who knows the regulator's exception format.

controls: must be filed by the 10th business day

spofs: Priya is the only reviewer who knows the regulator's exception format

tacit_knowledge: regulator's exception format known by Priya

tasks.description: Messy high-stakes utterance with restart, correction, hedging, systems, escalation, and approval threshold.
turns: So credit holds, actually we call it credit release now -- AR owns it. It runs, um, several times a day I think. NetSuite for sure, Sales pings in Slack when orders are blocked, and if it's over $100k, no release until VP Finance approves.

controls: orders over $100k cannot be released until VP Finance approves

tasks.description: Safety incident reporting with compliance deadline, escalation, and documentation.
turns: Warehouse safety incident reporting is owned by EHS. Supervisors log incidents in Intelex within 24 hours, serious injuries go to Legal immediately, and OSHA recordability is reviewed weekly by the EHS manager.
